r0030: 14.  On 27 October 1994 the applicant was brought before the substitute judge at the İstanbul National Security Court (*cour de sûreté de l’Etat*), who ordered his detention on remand. Before the judge, the applicant stated that he had committed two armed robberies and one attempted armed robbery, at a bank and two jewellers’ shops, in order to raise funds for an illegal organisation, the TKEP/TKP (Communist Workers’ Party of Turkey – Communist Party of Kurdistan).
r0031: 15.  On 29 November 1994 the public prosecutor at the İstanbul National Security Court (*cour de sûreté de l’Etat*) indicted the applicant before that court, which was composed of three professional judges, one of whom was a member of the military judiciary. Accusing the applicant of having attempted to overthrow the Turkish constitutional order by force, he sought the application of Article 146 of the Criminal Code (*code pénal*) and section 5 of the Prevention of Terrorism Act (Law no. 3713) (*loi sur la lutte contre le terrorisme*).
r0032: 16.  In a judgment of 4 March 1997, the National Security Court (*cour de sûreté de l’Etat*) found the applicant guilty of the offences with which he had been charged and sentenced him to life imprisonment (that is, in practice, in accordance with section 19 of the Execution of Sentences Act (Law no. 647) (*loi sur l’exécution des peines*), twenty years’ actual imprisonment followed by sixteen years’ conditional release). In its judgment, the court noted that during the investigation the applicant had admitted the offences in question, that he had been identified by the jeweller and the shop’s employees and that the statements of his co-accused, C.A., confirmed the version of the facts as set out in the indictment.
r0033: 17.  On 5 March 1997 the applicant appealed on points of law against the judgment, requesting a public hearing.
r0034: 18.  On 6 June 1997 the public prosecutor transmitted the case file to the Court of Cassation (*Cour de cassation*), together with his written observations, in which he sought the upholding of the applicant’s conviction.
r0035: 19.  On 15 January 1998, after holding a hearing, the Court of Cassation (*Cour de cassation*) upheld the impugned judgment.
r0036: II.  RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND PRACTICE
r0037: 20.  Before the amendment of 18 June 1999, the relevant part of Article 143 of the Constitution, governing the judicial organisation of national security courts (*cours de sûreté de l’Etat*), read as follows:
r0038: “National security courts (*cours de sûreté de l’Etat*) shall be established to try persons accused of offences against the Republic – whose constituent qualities are enunciated in the Constitution –, against the territorial integrity of the State or the indivisible unity of the nation, or against the free and democratic system of government, and offences directly affecting the State’s internal or external security.
r0039: National security courts (*cours de sûreté de l’Etat*) shall consist of a president, two full members, two substitute members, a public prosecutor and a sufficient number of assistant prosecutors.
